newsitem.title: USA: Ingersoll-Rand reports higher second-quarter net.
newsitem.headline: Ingersoll-Rand reports higher second-quarter net.

text.p: Ingersoll-Rand Co., the industrial equipment and components maker, Wednesday reported record second-quarter profits, fuelled by a stronger economy and successful cost-cutting efforts.

The company said profits climbed 20 percent for the quarter, to $111.6 million, or $1.03 a share, compared with $92.3 million, or 86 cents a share, a year ago. The results beat Wall Street's forecast of 96 cents a share, based on estimates compiled by First Call.
Sales for the second quarter of 1997 totalled $1.8 billion, an increase of 4 percent from last year's second quarter, with much of the improvement seen in the United States.

"We attribute this record second-quarter performance to a strong domestic economy, supplemented by continuing benefits of internal procurement and cost-containment programmes," said James Perrella, chairman, president and chief executive officer.
Virtually all of Ingersoll's major businesses reported higher operating income for the quarter, led by strong growth in its standard machinery and bearings, locks, and tools segments.

Income from its standard machinery division climbed 12 percent, to $112.2 million for the quarter, on sales of $834.5 million. Ingersoll said strength in the U.S. construction market, as well as productivity improvements, more than offset continued sluggishness in the company's European markets.
Sales of bearings, locks and tools totalled $781.7 million, up 25 percent from last year's second quarter. The division's operating income also climbed 25 percent, to $93.3 million.
Ingersoll's stock rose $1.125 to $63.56 in late consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
